claim: UA-ChatDev estimates per-agent-response uncertainty using token-level log probabilities, not execution/test-verified confidence, to decide when to trigger retrieval-based verification in a multi-agent software development pipeline.
stance_target: UA-ChatDev is PARTIAL/distinct occupancy vs per-test-case execution-verified structured confidence
scope_conditions: multi-agent LLM software development frameworks (ChatDev-style role-based agents)
quoted_support: It introduces a lightweight uncertainty estimation mechanism based on token-level log probabilities to assess the confidence of agent responses and employs phase-aware threshold calibration to selectively trigger retrieval-based verification when uncertainty exceeds acceptable levels.

claim: UA-ChatDev's granularity is per-development-phase/per-agent-response (requirements, coding, testing), not per-test-case within a single generation problem.
quoted_support: existing approaches typically assume that intermediate agent outputs are equally reliable, leaving them vulnerable to hallucination propagation, where incorrect decisions generated in early development phases are transferred to downstream agents

claim: UA-ChatDev outperforms single-agent and multi-agent software development baselines on completeness, executability, consistency, and overall quality metrics on the SRDD benchmark.
stance_target: effectiveness of uncertainty-aware multi-agent code generation
quoted_support: Extensive experiments on the SRDD benchmark demonstrate that UA-ChatDev consistently outperforms existing single-agent and multi-agent software development frameworks across completeness, executability, consistency, and overall quality metrics.
